newsitem.title: USA: N.Dakota wheat gets more rain, but condition ebbs.
newsitem.headline: N.Dakota wheat gets more rain, but condition ebbs.

text.p: Showers and thunderstorms brought more relief to North Dakota crops during the week ended June 29, the state's agricultural statistics service said Monday in its weekly crop progress report.

But the report said crop conditions of small grains fell off despite the rains. Topsoil moisture was replenished but conditions continued to be much drier than last year and the 5-year average. Condition of corn, soybeans, sugarbeets and dry beans improved during the week, the report said.
Topsoil moisture conditions improved and were rated 44 percent short to very short, against 61 in that category last week, 15 percent last year and the average of 19 percent.
Forty-three percent of the state's spring wheat crop rated good or excellent, down from 45 at that level last week. Durum was rated 26 percent good to excellent, against 34 last week.
Spring wheat was 75 percent jointing, against 48 a week ago, 59 a year ago, and 76 on the five-year average.
